segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ מִשֶּׁקָּרַב הָעוֹמֶר הוּתַּר חָדָשׁ מִיָּד, הָרְחוֹקִים מוּתָּרִין מֵחֲצוֹת הַיּוֹם וּלְהַלָּן. מִשֶּׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ, הִתְקִין רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי שֶׁיְּהֵא יוֹם הֶנֶף כּוּלּוֹ אָסוּר.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «From» the moment «that the omer» offering «was sacrificed,» the produce of the «new» crop «was permitted immediately.» For those «distant» from Jerusalem, the new crop «is permitted from midday and beyond. From» the time «that the Temple was destroyed, Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai instituted that the day of waving» the omer, the sixteenth of Nisan, «is entirely prohibited,» i.e., one may partake of the new crop only the next day.

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: וַהֲלֹא מִן הַתּוֹרָה הוּא אָסוּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״עַד עֶצֶם הַיּוֹם הַזֶּה״, מִפְּנֵי מָה הָרְחוֹקִים מוּתָּרִין מֵחֲצוֹת הַיּוֹם וּלְהַלָּן? מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהֵן יוֹדְעִין שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין מִתְעַצְּלִין בּוֹ.
segments.en: «Rabbi Yehuda said: But isn’t it forbidden by Torah law, as it is stated:» “And you shall eat neither bread, nor parched grain, nor fresh grain, «until this selfsame day,» until you have brought the offering of your God” (Leviticus 23:14)? This means that the new crop is prohibited on the day of the waving unless permitted by sacrifice of the offering. «And» if so, «for what» reason is it «permitted» for those «distant» to eat the new crop «from midday and beyond,» when the Temple is standing? It is «due to» the fact «that they know that the» members of the «court are not indolent in its» sacrifice, and certainly by midday the sacrifice of the omer offering has been completed.
